LAREDO, Texas — Robert Jerry Jimenez was arrested Thursday evening, October 22, 2026, and booked into the Webb County Jail on multiple alleged felony charges, including child endangerment, burglary of a habitation, evading arrest with a vehicle, and manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance, according to Webb County booking records.

Jimenez, 20, was arrested at 6:57 p.m. by the Laredo Police Department. The booking record reviewed by Webb Watch 956 listed seven charges — six felonies and one misdemeanor. Four of the felony charges, including two counts of abandoning or endangering a child, evading arrest or detention with a vehicle, and burglary of a habitation with intent to commit another felony, were warrant arrests tied to an offense date in February 2024. The remaining charges, including alleged manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance in penalty group 1 in an amount of 4 to 200 grams and possession of a controlled substance in penalty group 2 in an amount of 1 to 4 grams, stemmed from a warrantless arrest on October 22.

Bond had not been set on any of the charges as of the booking record reviewed by Webb Watch 956. No holds were listed.

A first-degree felony in Texas is punishable by five to 99 years or life in prison and a fine of up to $10,000.

An arrest is an allegation, not a conviction. Robert Jerry Jimenez is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff's Office Booking Jail Search; Webb County public-access court records.
